machinelearning.train_test_splits
=================================

.. py:module:: machinelearning.train_test_splits

.. autoapi-nested-parse::

   Manually create a pandas dataframe with the
   following column name:
   - participant_id
   in order to split the data into disjoint sets:
    training, validation and test sets.

.. py:function:: create_balanced_set(features_set: pandas.DataFrame) -> pandas.DataFrame

   # make sure that all participant IDs in test_set contribute
   # with the same number of rows by finding the minimum number
   # of rows per participant in the test set and excluding the
   # lowest-quality rows from participants with more rows than the minimum

    Keeps, for each participant, the rows with the highest quality_indicator values instead of arbitrarily taking the first rows. It sorts by participant_id and quality_indicator descending, then keeps the top rows up to the minimum per-participant count. If quality_indicator is missing, it now raises a clear error.


.. py:function:: find_missing_participant_ids(df: pandas.DataFrame, participant_col: str = 'participant_id', start: int = 0) -> list[str]

   Finds missing participant IDs.

   Supports IDs such as:
       ieb_03, ieb_04, ...
       id01, id05, ...
       1, 2, 4, 5, ...

   :param start: First ID to consider when searching for missing values.
   :type start: int

   :returns: Missing participant IDs.
   :rtype: list[str]


.. py:function:: convert_participant_ids(df: pandas.DataFrame) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Converts participant IDs to a consistent format.
   It converts from #001 to hu_01, #002 to hu_02, etc.
   :returns: Dataframe with converted participant IDs.
   :rtype: pd.DataFrame

.. py:function:: create_random_splits_and_write_participants_list(output_folder: str, df: pandas.DataFrame, train_pct: float = 0.7, val_pct: float = 0.15, test_pct: float = 0.15, random_state: int = 42) -> None

   Splits participants into train/validation/test sets based on percentages.

   :param datasetConfig: config object with output path
   :param df: dataframe containing a 'participant_id' column
   :param train_pct: must sum to 1.0
   :param val_pct: must sum to 1.0
   :param test_pct: must sum to 1.0
   :param random_state: for reproducibility


.. py:function:: create_stratified_glc_splits_and_write_participants_list(output_folder: str, df: pandas.DataFrame, train_pct: float = 0.7, val_pct: float = 0.15, test_pct: float = 0.15, random_state: int = 42, low_threshold: float = 70.0, high_threshold: float = 180.0, participant_col: str = 'participant_id', glc_col: str = 'GLC', aggregation: str = 'median') -> None

   Splits participants into train/validation/test sets disjoint by participant_id,
   stratified by glucose class derived from GLC.

   Glucose classes:
       low    : GLC < low_threshold
       normal : low_threshold <= GLC <= high_threshold
       high   : GLC > high_threshold

   Since each participant may have many GLC samples, one participant-level GLC
   value is first computed using aggregation, e.g., median or mean.

   :param output_folder: Folder where participant lists will be written.
   :type output_folder: str
   :param df: Dataframe containing participant_id and GLC columns.
   :type df: pd.DataFrame
   :param train_pct: Split percentages. Must sum to 1.
   :type train_pct: float
   :param val_pct: Split percentages. Must sum to 1.
   :type val_pct: float
   :param test_pct: Split percentages. Must sum to 1.
   :type test_pct: float
   :param random_state: Random seed for reproducibility.
   :type random_state: int
   :param low_threshold: Threshold below which glucose is classified as low.
   :type low_threshold: float
   :param high_threshold: Threshold above which glucose is classified as high.
   :type high_threshold: float
   :param participant_col: Name of the participant ID column.
   :type participant_col: str
   :param glc_col: Name of the glucose column.
   :type glc_col: str
   :param aggregation: Participant-level GLC aggregation: "median" or "mean".
   :type aggregation: str


.. py:function:: run_fixed_split_for_dataset_ieb3(datasetConfig)

.. py:function:: format_metadata(df: pandas.DataFrame) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Ensures that the dataframe has a column named 'participant_id'.
   If it has a column named 'participant', it renames it to 'participant_id'.
   Raises an error if neither column is present.
